record.paper_title: Open problems of the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Does every bridgeless graph admit a pair of flows consisting of a 2-flow φ_2 and a 4-flow φ_4 such that for every edge e, whenever φ_2(e)=0 one has |φ_4(e)| ≥ 2?

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 6.1 Each bridgeless graph admits a 2-flow ϕ2 and a 4-flow ϕ4 such that for
any edge e, if ϕ2(e) = 0, then |ϕ4(e)| ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite bridgeless graph (loops and multiple edges allowed). Fix an arbitrary orientation of the edges of G. For an integer k ≥ 2, a k-flow on G is an assignment φ : E(G) → {−(k−1), …, −1, 0, 1, …, k−1} such that at every vertex the sum of φ-values on outgoing edges equals the sum of φ-values on incoming edges (Kirchhoff's law). The values φ(e) are integers and the flow need not be nowhere-zero.

Prove or disprove: every bridgeless graph G admits a pair (φ₂, φ₄) consisting of a 2-flow φ₂ and a 4-flow φ₄ on G such that for every edge e ∈ E(G), if φ₂(e) = 0 then |φ₄(e)| ≥ 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture in a recent open-problems collection from a workshop on cycles and colourings. Web searches for related flow-pair statements turn up classical Tutte flow conjectures and recent work on non-conflicting Z₂×Z₂ flows in cubic graphs, but no resolution of this specific pair-of-flows conjecture. No source claiming a proof or counterexample was found, so the problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: 4-flow conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: Every bridgeless graph with no Petersen minor admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow.
status_evidence.claim: Related classical 4-flow conjecture remains open in general; no mention of the pair-of-flows version being resolved.

status_evidence.title: Non-conflicting no-where zero Z2Z2 flows in cubic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on pairs of compatible flows in cubic graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related questions about coordinated pairs of flows are an active area, with no resolution of the stated conjecture.
